NDT training in Wichita: how it works for Wichita employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Wichita employers and technicians. Theory runs live online, and practicals run onsite at your facility, whether that is an aerostructures supplier, a machine shop, a refinery contractor or a pipeline inspection company. Level I, II and III courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer then certifies you under its own written practice.

Wichita is not a typical NDT market. Most American cities that search for NDT training are refinery or pipeline towns, where nearly every technician works to ASME and API 1104. In the Air Capital, a large share of NDT work is aerospace: airframe structures, composites, machined aluminium and titanium, and landing-gear steel. Much of that is certified under the aerospace primes' own schemes rather than under SNT-TC-1A alone. Around the aerospace cluster sits a very conventional industrial market: refining in Butler County, crude and product pipelines across the state, pressure-vessel and tank fabrication, agricultural-equipment and HVAC manufacturing, and power generation. That industrial market runs on SNT-TC-1A.

We think the most useful thing this page can do is explain which part of that market our training fits and where it does not. The short version: SNT-TC-1A training from Atlantis gives Wichita technicians solid method knowledge and gives industrial employers certifiable training records. Aerospace employers who certify to NAS 410 run their own scheme on top. It is also worth saying plainly that Atlantis has no training centre in Wichita. Theory is delivered live online, and practical training is delivered onsite at your facility, on your equipment and your parts.

If you already know what you need, request a Wichita training quote. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Wichita

Every course is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Recommended classroom and experience hours for each method and level are in our training-requirements matrix. Your written practice sets the hours that actually apply to you, and it may be stricter.

MethodLevelsWhat Wichita employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic)I, II, III prepThickness and weld examination for refinery, pipeline and vessel work; bond and laminate inspection concepts for composite and metallic aerostructures; forging and bar-stock inspection in machine shopsNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
PAUT (phased array)II, III prepEncoded weld examination on pipelines and vessels, corrosion mapping at refinery and terminal sites, rapid scanning of large structural areasUT Level II or equivalent UT knowledge accepted by the written practice
TOFDII, III prepThick-section weld sizing on pressure vessels and heavy-wall piping, usually paired with PAUTUT Level II
RT (radiographic)I, II, III prepCastings and weldments in manufacturing, pipeline girth welds, vessel seams; film and digital radiographyNone for Level I; radiation-safety training and radiographer certification are separate legal requirements
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, III prepSteel forgings and machined parts, agricultural and oilfield equipment, structural welds, pipeline dig sites; bench (wet horizontal) units in production shopsNone for Level I
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, III prepNon-magnetic machined parts (aluminium, titanium, stainless), castings, weld surfaces; fluorescent penetrant lines in manufacturingNone for Level I
VT (visual)I, II, III prepWeld visual to AWS D1.1 and ASME, in-service visual on tanks and vessels, incoming and in-process inspection in fabricationNone for Level I
ET (eddy current)I, II, III prepSurface and near-surface crack detection, conductivity and coating-thickness checks on aluminium, bolt-hole and fastener-site inspection concepts, heat-exchanger tubing in industrial plantsNone for Level I

UT. The course covers sound propagation, transducer and wedge selection, calibration, straight-beam and angle-beam techniques, and DAC and TCG. It then turns to interpretation against the acceptance criteria your work uses. For Wichita industrial candidates the course addresses ASME and API 1104 weld work. For manufacturing candidates it addresses inspection of forgings, plate and bar. Technicians heading for aerospace work get the physics grounding that composite and bonded-structure inspection depends on: attenuation, near-surface resolution and through-transmission versus pulse-echo. The employer's own aerospace procedures and qualification then take over from there.

PAUT and TOFD. These come after conventional UT. The courses cover focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded data collection and analysis, and TOFD geometry and sizing. In Kansas, PAUT and TOFD are mostly used on pipeline, terminal and refinery work rather than in the aerospace plants. That makes them a sensible specialisation for a UT technician who wants the industrial side of the market.

RT. The course covers X-ray and gamma sources, exposure technique, film and digital detectors, image quality, and interpretation of casting and weld discontinuities. Cabinet and fixed-installation X-ray work in manufacturing, and field gamma radiography on pipelines, carry different radiation-safety obligations. We explain both in the regulator section below.

MT and PT. In Wichita these are often production methods, not only field methods. Parts move through a wet-bench MT unit or a fluorescent-penetrant line on a schedule. The courses cover the principles plus the process-control side: bath concentration, UV-A intensity, ambient visible light, dwell and development times, and system performance checks. A technician who understands why each check exists does much better in a production audit than one who has memorised the steps.

VT. The course covers visual acuity requirements, lighting, optical aids, weld gauges and acceptance criteria. For fabrication shops VT is the gatekeeper method, and most problems that get past it are later found by a more expensive method.

ET. The course covers electromagnetic principles, the impedance plane, frequency selection, reference standards and probe types. In Wichita, ET technicians work on non-ferrous materials. That includes crack detection, conductivity and coating-thickness measurement on aluminium parts, and tube inspection in the region's industrial plants.

Level III. Experienced Level IIs aiming for procedure-writing and certifying roles can follow our ASNT Level III preparation, which covers the Basic exam and method exams. ASNT administers the Level III exams itself.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Wichita, step by step

  1. Identify the written practice. Your employer's written practice controls the whole process, including hours, exams, grading, vision requirements and recertification. If your target employer certifies to an aerospace standard rather than SNT-TC-1A, find that out before you book anything.
  2. Complete formal training. Classroom hours for the method and level, live online or onsite, fully documented. Compare the training-requirements matrix with your written practice.
  3. Accumulate documented experience. Supervised hours in the method, logged and signed. On a production line the hours come quickly. The discipline that matters is getting them recorded in a form an auditor will accept.
  4. General examination. Written exam on the principles of the method, given under a Level III.
  5. Specific examination. Written exam on the employer's own procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on exam on specimens containing real discontinuities. You demonstrate set-up, examination, interpretation and reporting.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast. Near vision is re-checked at least annually.
  8. Employer certification. The employer certifies you in writing, based on the documented results.
  9. Recertification. Follows the interval your written practice sets (SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum of five years), and certification can lapse if you stop working in the method. A new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice.

For a fuller explanation, see our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Wichita crews

There are three delivery options for Wichita, and we will tell you plainly which one suits you:

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions for the classroom hours. This suits shift workers in manufacturing plants and field technicians travelling between refinery, pipeline and terminal jobs across Kansas and Oklahoma. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. Practical training and exams at your plant or shop, on your instruments and your parts. For a manufacturer with a penetrant line or MT bench, this is the only sensible approach, because the practical should test the process your technicians run every day.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by a concentrated onsite practical block. This is common for multi-method programmes.

Scheduling follows Wichita's rhythms. Manufacturing plants usually prefer training during planned slowdowns or across shift patterns rather than taking a whole crew off the line. Refinery and pipeline contractors are busiest during turnarounds and the construction season. We plan around both and can run theory in evening blocks. For multi-site employers, corporate NDT training explains how programmes are sequenced.

Practical exams are never done remotely. Ask about onsite training for your Wichita crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Wichita

Aerospace manufacturing and the supply chain. Wichita's aircraft makers and aerostructures plants are the largest concentration of NDT demand in the city. Behind them is a deep tier of suppliers doing machining, sheet metal, composites, heat treating, plating and assembly. Most suppliers in that chain run production NDT: fluorescent penetrant, wet MT, eddy current, ultrasonic and radiography of parts and assemblies. Aerospace primes typically flow down NAS 410 personnel certification and require special-process approvals such as Nadcap. Atlantis does not train or certify to NAS 410. If your employer works under NAS 410, its own programme governs your certification. The method theory in our SNT-TC-1A courses can still be useful background for technicians new to NDT or moving across from industrial work, but it is not a substitute for the prime's required scheme.

Military aviation. McConnell Air Force Base in southeast Wichita is home to an air refuelling wing flying tankers. Military NDT follows the service's own technical orders and personnel programmes, which are separate from the civilian SNT-TC-1A system. Some contractors supporting military aviation do use SNT-TC-1A for their personnel, which is one of the ways Wichita's civil and military NDT markets overlap.

Aviation research and education. Wichita State University's aviation research institute and the region's technical college aviation programmes train and employ people in materials testing and inspection. These are strong local pipelines for talent. They are independent of Atlantis, and we mention them only as part of the local landscape.

Refining, pipelines and energy. A refinery at El Dorado, northeast of Wichita, is one of the larger inland refineries in the region. Wichita is also home to major energy and commodity businesses, and Kansas is crossed by crude oil, refined product and natural gas pipelines, with storage terminals and compressor stations along them. This work runs on ASME B31.3 and Section VIII for plant piping and vessels, API 1104 for pipeline welding, and API 650/653 for storage tanks. Pipelines are also regulated federally under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, which bring their own operator-qualification requirements. UT thickness, PAUT corrosion mapping, RT on girth welds, and MT/PT at digs and on tanks are the methods in demand. Some employers here also ask for API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certifications or CWI. Those are separate schemes that we do not train.

General manufacturing and fabrication. Beyond aerospace, the Wichita area makes HVAC equipment, agricultural machinery, oil-field equipment, trailers and structural steel. Welds are made to AWS D1.1 or ASME, castings and forgings are checked with MT and PT, and pressure-retaining products go through RT or UT. These employers usually run SNT-TC-1A written practices and are the most natural fit for our training.

Power generation. Utility generating stations across Kansas, including a nuclear station in the eastern part of the state, need outage NDT: UT on piping and headers, MT and PT on components, and ET on condenser and heat-exchanger tubes. Commercial nuclear in-service inspection uses additional personnel-qualification requirements, including CP-189 and performance demonstration for certain UT. Nuclear employers will say what they need.

Radiography licensing in Kansas. Kansas is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials used in industrial radiography, such as iridium-192 and selenium-75 cameras, are licensed and inspected by the Kansas Department of Health and Environment (KDHE) radiation control programme rather than by the NRC. KDHE also oversees radiation-producing machines such as industrial X-ray units. Anyone using a gamma camera must hold radiographer certification (typically through the ASNT Industrial Radiography Radiation Safety Personnel programme or a recognised state programme) and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. Out-of-state companies bringing sources into Kansas must meet the state's reciprocity requirements. SNT-TC-1A RT certification covers technique and interpretation. It does not authorise you to handle sources.

What Wichita employers ask for. Industrial and fabrication employers most often want SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT, MT, PT and VT, with RT for pipeline and vessel work and PAUT for advanced roles. Aerospace employers ask for experience with their own scheme and production methods such as fluorescent PT and ET. For typical pay by level, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Wichita NDT companies

Wichita has many small and mid-sized shops that do NDT as one step in a larger manufacturing process, and many of them have no Level III on the payroll. Their customers still audit their NDT, and SNT-TC-1A still requires a written practice, Level III-administered exams and records that hold up. Atlantis supports them in four ways:

  • Written-practice development. We draft or revise your written practice for the methods and levels you actually run, aligned with current SNT-TC-1A and your customers' purchase-order requirements. See NDT written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Exam preparation and administration, procedure and technique-sheet approval, and review of existing certification files before a customer audit.
  • Process-control reviews. For shops with penetrant lines or MT benches, we check that daily and periodic system checks are specified and recorded in the way your procedures say they are.
  • SNT-TC-1A guidance. Our SNT-TC-1A certification page explains employer-based certification for quality managers.

Book a Level III consultation and tell us your methods, headcount and the customer requirements you have to meet.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The hangar environment is a natural fit for Wichita technicians, and the lab, workshop and tank scenarios match the city's industrial work. Trainees can rehearse set-ups, scan coverage and indication recognition as often as they like between sessions.

It is a practice tool only. It does not replace hands-on training with real equipment or the practical exam on real specimens that your written practice requires.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. As Level III he oversees course content, exam design and practical assessment, and onsite programmes for Wichita employers run under that oversight.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Wichita

How do I get NDT certified in Wichita?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete formal training, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and supports employers with written practices and Level III services. If your employer is an aerospace company certifying to NAS 410, its own programme applies instead.

Can I take NDT training online in Kansas?

Yes, for theory. Live online sessions cover the classroom hours. Practical training and exams must be done hands-on, onsite at your employer's facility or in a scheduled practical block. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom and experience hours in your employer's written practice and on whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimums, which are listed in our training-requirements matrix. The experience hours usually take longer than the classroom.

Do I need a license for radiography in Kansas?

Kansas is an Agreement State, so the Kansas Department of Health and Environment licenses radioactive materials used in industrial radiography and oversees X-ray equipment. Radiographers using sources must hold radiographer certification and work under the licensee's radiation-safety programme. SNT-TC-1A RT certification is a separate requirement covering technique and interpretation.

What does NDT training cost in Wichita?

We do not publish prices. The cost depends on the method, the level, the group size and whether training is online, onsite or blended. We return cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request a Wichita training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Wichita employers?

Yes, by most industrial, fabrication, pipeline, refinery and power employers, for whom SNT-TC-1A is the normal basis for certification. Aerospace primes and their suppliers usually certify under NAS 410, so check the scheme with the employer before you train.

Do you offer NAS 410 aerospace NDT certification?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. NAS 410 certification is run by the aerospace employer under its own programme. Our method courses can give newcomers useful theory, but they do not replace the employer's NAS 410 qualification.

Which NDT method should I start with in Wichita?

For production manufacturing, PT and MT are the most common first methods, with ET and UT close behind. For industrial field work, MT, PT and VT plus UT are a good base, and RT is added for pipeline work. Specialise once you know which side of the market you are aiming at.

Can you train our shop's technicians onsite?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility is our standard model for employers, with practicals on your equipment and parts. Ask about onsite training for your Wichita crew.

We have no Level III. Can Atlantis act as ours?

Yes. Outsourced Level III services include written-practice development, exam administration and procedure approval. See written practice development.

How can I prepare for a Level II exam?

Study the method theory, use mock exams such as our UT Level 2 practice questions, and rehearse set-ups on the Practical NDT simulator before the hands-on practical.

Do you train for API or CWI certifications?

No. Some Wichita-area refinery and tank employers ask for API 510, 570 or 653 or CWI. Those are separate schemes with their own bodies. We train the SNT-TC-1A method certifications that sit alongside them.
